Use the bundled synthetic data to check inputs, fit expected counts, calculate and plot SPI, and produce annually updated estimates. [Interpreting SPI alongside AFP indicators](spi-interpretation.html) explains what the results mean.

The outputs shown here were computed with INLA when the article was built.

## Input data

spi needs three inputs, all using the same district ID column:

- monthly NPAFP case counts, one row per district and month;
- annual under-15 population, one row per district and year;
- district boundaries as an `sf` object.

The bundled `synth_surveillance` data cover 236 districts in the fictional country Harad, from 2015 to 2024. The district ID column is `adm2_guid`:


``` r
library(spi)
synth <- synth_surveillance

names(synth$cases)
#> [1] "adm2_guid" "month"     "count"
names(synth$population)
#> [1] "adm2_guid" "year"      "pop_u15"
names(synth$boundaries)
#> [1] "adm2_guid" "adm2_name" "adm1_name" "adm0_name" "geom"
```

`month` is the first day of each month, `count` is the number of NPAFP cases reported in that month, and `pop_u15` is the under-15 population for the year. Months with no cases should be present with a count of zero.

### Check the inputs first

Use `spi_check_inputs()` to check case counts, population denominators, and district boundaries before fitting the model. It reports mismatched district IDs, missing months, and other issues as errors, warnings, or notes. `spi_expected()` also runs this check and stops on errors.


``` r
spi_check_inputs(
  cases = synth$cases,
  population = synth$population,
  shapefile = synth$boundaries,
  id_col = "adm2_guid"
)
#>
#> -- spi input check -------------------------------------------------------------
#> v All input checks passed -- 236 districts x 120 months (2015-01 to 2024-12).
```

Here is the report for data with one negative count and three missing months:


``` r
bad_cases <- synth$cases |>
  # set the first count to -1 to simulate a data-entry error
  dplyr::mutate(
    count = dplyr::if_else(dplyr::row_number() == 1, -1, count)
  ) |>
  # remove three district-months to simulate missing records
  dplyr::slice(-(2:4))

spi_check_inputs(
  cases = bad_cases,
  population = synth$population,
  shapefile = synth$boundaries,
  id_col = "adm2_guid"
)
#>
#> -- spi input check -------------------------------------------------------------
#> i 236 districts x 120 months (2015-01 to 2024-12)
#> x 1 case row has negative counts
#> ! 3 district-months missing from the panel (gaps)
#> --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#> x 1 error -- resolve before fitting.
```

## Fit expected counts

`spi_expected()` fits the default model to all supplied years. Passing the district boundaries as `adjacency` builds the neighbour graph internally. `n_draws` sets the number of posterior draws kept for the SPI intervals, and `seed` makes the draws reproducible. Fitting requires INLA and can take several minutes.


``` r
fit <- spi_expected(
  cases = synth$cases,
  population = synth$population,
  adjacency = synth$boundaries,
  id_col = "adm2_guid",
  n_draws = 500,
  seed = 42,
  verbose = FALSE
)
```

The fitted object contains posterior draws and summaries for each district-month. View observed counts, expected medians, and 90% credible intervals:


``` r
fit |>
  tibble::as_tibble() |>
  dplyr::filter(count > 0) |>
  dplyr::select(
    adm2_guid, month, count,
    expected_median, expected_q05, expected_q95
  ) |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 6)
#> # A tibble: 6 x 6
#>   adm2_guid           month      count expected_median expected_q05 expected_q95
#>   <chr>               <date>     <int>           <dbl>        <dbl>        <dbl>
#> 1 {54CD979C-CF9D-6A6~ 2015-06-01     1           0.518        0.430        0.629
#> 2 {54CD979C-CF9D-6A6~ 2015-11-01     1           0.577        0.480        0.699
#> 3 {54CD979C-CF9D-6A6~ 2016-01-01     2           0.787        0.646        0.957
#> 4 {54CD979C-CF9D-6A6~ 2016-02-01     1           0.800        0.658        0.969
#> 5 {54CD979C-CF9D-6A6~ 2016-04-01     1           0.734        0.606        0.895
#> 6 {54CD979C-CF9D-6A6~ 2016-05-01     1           0.676        0.560        0.826
```

## Calculate SPI

`spi_index()` sums observed and expected counts to the chosen level and calculates SPI for each posterior draw. Use annual SPI for review, because monthly AFP counts are often sparse. Monthly SPI is more useful for descriptive trends.


``` r
spi_year <- spi_index(fit, level = "district_year", centre = "national")
spi_raw <- spi_index(fit, level = "district_year", centre = "none")
spi_month <- spi_index(fit, level = "district_month")
```

With `centre = "national"`, the default, each district's observed-to-expected ratio is divided by the national ratio for the same period. With `centre = "none"`, SPI is the district's own observed-to-expected ratio. [Interpreting SPI](spi-interpretation.html#national-centring) explains the difference with a worked example.

## Understand the output

`as_tibble()` returns one row per district and period. `observed` is the reported count for the period. `spi_median` is the posterior median of SPI, and `spi_q05` and `spi_q95` bound its 90% credible interval. The interval reflects uncertainty in expected counts, holding observed counts fixed.


``` r
spi_year |>
  tibble::as_tibble() |>
  dplyr::select(adm2_guid, year, observed, spi_median, spi_q05, spi_q95) |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 6)
#> # A tibble: 6 x 6
#>   adm2_guid                             year observed spi_median spi_q05 spi_q95
#>   <chr>                                <dbl>    <int>      <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>
#> 1 {01325AA0-BEA1-66FE-9B5C-88AA603382~  2015        1      0.679   0.481   0.943
#> 2 {01325AA0-BEA1-66FE-9B5C-88AA603382~  2016        2      1.11    0.786   1.55
#> 3 {01325AA0-BEA1-66FE-9B5C-88AA603382~  2017        0      0       0       0
#> 4 {01325AA0-BEA1-66FE-9B5C-88AA603382~  2018        2      0.990   0.702   1.38
#> 5 {01325AA0-BEA1-66FE-9B5C-88AA603382~  2019        5      2.14    1.50    2.96
#> 6 {01325AA0-BEA1-66FE-9B5C-88AA603382~  2020        2      1.50    1.07    2.10
```

`spi_year$national` reports the national observed-to-expected ratio for each year (`national_oe`). Centred SPI divides each district's ratio by this value, so review it separately: district SPI can stay unchanged when district and national ratios change together.


``` r
spi_year$national
#> # A tibble: 10 x 5
#>     year national_observed national_expected national_oe districts
#>    <dbl>             <int>             <dbl>       <dbl>     <int>
#>  1  2015              3468             3508.       0.989       236
#>  2  2016              4228             4234.       0.999       236
#>  3  2017              4373             4421.       0.989       236
#>  4  2018              4768             4794.       0.995       236
#>  5  2019              5558             5442.       1.02        236
#>  6  2020              3153             3179.       0.992       236
#>  7  2021              3372             3432.       0.982       236
#>  8  2022              4578             4461.       1.03        236
#>  9  2023              5246             5316.       0.987       236
#> 10  2024              6085             5844.       1.04        236
```

`summary()` gives diagnostics across all district-years, including the median SPI, the overall observed-to-expected ratio, and the share of credible intervals that exclude 1. A `flag` marks a diagnostic outside the range set by the package, as a prompt to look more closely:


``` r
summary(spi_year)
#> # A tibble: 12 x 3
#>    metric                      value  flag
#>    <chr>                       <chr>  <chr>
#>  1 median SPI                  0.935  pass
#>  2 calibration ratio (obs/exp) 1.001  pass
#>  3 log-SPI skewness            -0.825 flag
#>  4 % with CrI excluding 1      74.7   flag
#>  5 % SPI < 0.5 (severe)        16.9   <NA>
#>  6 % SPI > 1.5 (elevated)      14.9   <NA>
#>  7 SPI q05                     0.095  <NA>
#>  8 SPI q25                     0.626  <NA>
#>  9 SPI q75                     1.286  <NA>
#> 10 SPI q95                     1.894  <NA>
#> 11 n groups                    2,360  <NA>
#> 12 n low_information           69     <NA>
```

## Plots

`plot()` offers four views. The default `distribution` view shows how SPI values are distributed relative to the reference value of 1:


``` r
plot(spi_year)
```

<img src="figures/getting-started-plot-distribution-1.png" alt="Histogram of district-year SPI values on a log scale, with reference lines at 0.5, 1 and 1.5." width="100%" />

The `funnel` view plots SPI against the expected count. Ratios based on small expected counts can vary widely, so inspect them with their credible intervals. Points are coloured by whether the district-year met the conventional NPAFP target:


``` r
plot(spi_year, type = "funnel")
```

<img src="figures/getting-started-plot-funnel-1.png" alt="Funnel plot of SPI against expected count, both on log scales, with points coloured by whether the NPAFP target was met." width="100%" />

The `caterpillar` view shows the lowest and highest SPI values with their credible intervals:


``` r
plot(spi_year, type = "caterpillar")
```

<img src="figures/getting-started-plot-caterpillar-1.png" alt="Caterpillar plot of the lowest and highest SPI district-years, each with its 90% credible interval." width="100%" />

The `calibration` view compares observed with expected counts. Points on the diagonal have observed counts equal to their expected counts:


``` r
plot(spi_year, type = "calibration")
```

<img src="figures/getting-started-plot-calibration-1.png" alt="Scatter of observed against expected counts on log scales, with a diagonal line of equality." width="100%" />

## Non-calendar years

Set `year_end_month` to use a reporting year other than January to December. With `year_end_month = 4`, each year runs from May to April and is labelled by the calendar year in which it closes, so May 2023 to April 2024 is 2024. The fitted model is unchanged; only the aggregation differs.


``` r
spi_may_apr <- spi_index(fit, level = "district_year", year_end_month = 4)

spi_may_apr |>
  tibble::as_tibble() |>
  dplyr::count(n_months, name = "district_years")
#> # A tibble: 3 x 2
#>   n_months district_years
#>      <int>          <int>
#> 1        4            236
#> 2        8            236
#> 3       12           2124
```

The first and last reporting periods may be incomplete. `n_months` shows how many months each period covers; periods with fewer than 12 months should normally be excluded.

## Prospective use

`spi_expected()` followed by `spi_index()` is a retrospective fit. The model uses the full period supplied, including the years being assessed, so a decline in an assessed year partly lowers that year's own expectation.

`spi_prospective()` refits the model for each assessment year using only the preceding years. This is how SPI would be updated each year in routine use, and it is the approach used in the accompanying study.


``` r
prospective <- spi_prospective(
  cases = synth$cases,
  population = synth$population,
  adjacency = synth$boundaries,
  first_assessment = 2019,
  last_assessment = 2024,
  id_col = "adm2_guid",
  n_draws = 500,
  seed = 42,
  verbose = FALSE
)
```

`prospective$prospective` lists the training years used for each assessment year:


``` r
prospective$prospective
#> # A tibble: 6 x 4
#>    year training_start training_end districts
#>   <int>          <int>        <int>     <int>
#> 1  2019           2015         2018       236
#> 2  2020           2015         2019       236
#> 3  2021           2015         2020       236
#> 4  2022           2015         2021       236
#> 5  2023           2015         2022       236
#> 6  2024           2015         2023       236
```

The result is a `spi_index` object at the district-year level, so `as_tibble()`, `summary()`, and `plot()` work as above. Use a consistent model specification, centring setting, and training approach when comparing years; do not mix retrospective and prospective estimates in one series.
